samples.summary: Text-box `getRangeStyleSummary` behavior change (raw run style → effective style with named-style defaults) has no test
samples.evidence: The diff replaces the text-box summary walk so each key is read from the *effective* style (`{...namedStyleDefaults, ...inline.style}`) instead of raw `inline.style`, and its comment claims this fixes the toolbar answering "not italic" for a run painted italic by its named style (heading-6 sets `italic: true`, packages/docs/src/model/named-styles.ts:91). I found no test asserting this for text boxes: packages/docs/test/view/text-box-editor.test.ts only touches getRangeStyleSummary for fontSize/pending-style stepping (lines ~809-816), and the slides consumer stubs it out entirely (packages/slides/test/view/editor/text-box-editor.test.ts:82 `getRangeStyleSummary: () => ({})`). The new packages/docs/test/view/backward-selection-toggle.test.ts exercises only `initialize` (the docs editor), never `initializeTextBox`. So the docs/slides text-box + shape + table-cell editors' summary change (and its knock-on effect on fontSize/color reported from title/heading blocks) can break without any test failing.

samples.summary: The `isStyleOnInSelection` fallback branch (range with no text runs, and the collapsed-caret + named-style-defaults path) is untested
samples.evidence: `applyStyle` now computes `!(inRange ?? !!effectiveVisual[key])`, so two new branches exist: (a) collapsed caret inside a block whose named style supplies the flag (e.g. Cmd+I with a bare caret in Heading 6 should stage `italic: false`), and (b) a non-empty selection that contains no text runs (empty block), where `isStyleOnInSelection` returns undefined and the caret style must be used. Every new keyboard test in packages/docs/test/view/backward-selection-toggle.test.ts sets a non-empty selection over non-empty runs (lines 168-199, 258-282, 380-397), and the pending-style tests (packages/docs/test/view/pending-style-editor.test.ts) call `editor.applyStyle({bold:true})` with explicit values rather than the toggle path, so neither branch is covered.

samples.summary: `stepSelectionFontSize`'s newly gained range coverage (cross-cell / body-to-cell endpoints, table read whole) is not tested
samples.evidence: Swapping the private collector for `visitStyledRunsInRange` changes which runs font-size stepping touches: cell endpoints now normalize to the parent table block and a table caught in a cross-block selection is stepped whole — cases the old `collectRunsInBlock` dispatch silently produced zero runs for. packages/docs/test/view/editor-step-selection-font-size.test.ts still only covers single-block, cross-block (same context), sub-range, clamping, collapsed caret and cell-range rectangle (test names at lines 111-239); no test spans two different cells or body→cell, so the newly reachable stepping behavior is unverified.

samples.summary: Weak negative assertions (`.not.toBe(true)`) pass even if the summary API returns nothing at all
samples.evidence: `expect(editor.getRangeStyleSummary().bold).not.toBe(true)` (line 153) and `expect(editor.getSelectionStyle().bold).not.toBe(true)` (line 162) hold for `undefined`, `'mixed'`, `false` — i.e. also in the failure mode where the walk collects no runs and the summary is empty, which is precisely the regression shape the surrounding tests describe. Asserting `false` (or the exact expected value) would make these tests able to fail for the right reason.

finding.summary: Text-box `getRangeStyleSummary` behavior change (raw run style → effective style with named-style defaults) has no test
finding.evidence: The diff replaces the text-box summary walk so each key is read from the *effective* style (`{...namedStyleDefaults, ...inline.style}`) instead of raw `inline.style`, and its comment claims this fixes the toolbar answering "not italic" for a run painted italic by its named style (heading-6 sets `italic: true`, packages/docs/src/model/named-styles.ts:91). I found no test asserting this for text boxes: packages/docs/test/view/text-box-editor.test.ts only touches getRangeStyleSummary for fontSize/pending-style stepping (lines ~809-816), and the slides consumer stubs it out entirely (packages/slides/test/view/editor/text-box-editor.test.ts:82 `getRangeStyleSummary: () => ({})`). verdict.reason: The text-box summary at packages/docs/src/view/text-box-editor.ts:1076 now reads each key from the named-style-layered effective style via the shared visitStyledRunsInRange walk (range-runs.ts:48), and its comment claims the "toolbar says not italic for a style-italic run" fix. No test exercises that branch: the only getRangeStyleSummary assertions on a real text box are packages/docs/test/view/text-box-editor.test.ts:812,815, which hit the collapsed-caret branch (text-box-editor.ts:1024-1041) that does not layer defaults at all; all other initializeTextBox users (text-box-composing, text-box-edit-link-in-place, text-box-link-trailing-edge, slides text-box-autofit-gating, text-box-click-scale) never call it; and every slides consumer stubs it (e.g. slides/test/view/editor/text-box-editor.test.ts:82, editor.test.ts:1267, hover-highlight.test.ts:31). Frontend tests only mock EditorAPI; there is no e2e suite. The one real counterexample I found covers the DOCS editor path only — editor-range-style-summary.test.ts:272-368 and backward-selection-toggle.test.ts:205-267 assert named-style defaults and the heading-6 italic summary, but both drive initialize() (editor.ts:2769), so they would all still pass if the text-box call site reverted to raw inline.style. That defeats the finding's secondary "title/heading fontSize/color knock-on" clause but not its core claim, so the missing-test gap for the text-box/shape/table-cell summary is real and blocking under the missing-tests rubric.

finding.summary: New cell→parent-table endpoint normalization (selection spanning two different cells, or a cell and a body block) is untested
finding.evidence: range-runs.ts:146-150 introduces `anchorTopId = anchorCI ? anchorCI.tableBlockId : ...` so a selection whose endpoints live in *different* cells (or one in a cell, one at top level) now resolves to the enclosing table block and produces a summary; previously `getBlockIndex` failed and the old code returned an empty summary. No test in packages/docs/test exercises a cross-cell or cell↔body selection against `getRangeStyleSummary()` or the Cmd+B path — the new header-table test only selects two blocks inside the *same* cell (backward-selection-toggle.test.ts, 'header table cell range summary' describe).

verdict.reason: The claimed-missing tests exist in the very file the reviewer says they read. packages/docs/test/view/backward-selection-toggle.test.ts:409-637 is a describe block 'cell endpoints normalize to the parent table (issue #715)' whose docblock (lines 400-408) names the exact normalization at range-runs.ts:157-158. It contains: a cross-cell selection asserting getRangeStyleSummary().bold === true (lines 471-482); the Cmd+B path on a cross-cell selection asserting both stored cell runs flip to bold:false (lines 484-500); a body-block-to-cell selection asserting the summary is 'mixed' (lines 502-513); and the Cmd+B path on that mixed body-to-cell selection asserting body and both cells become bold in the store (lines 515-533). Plus cell-rectangle toggles (535, 558) and a nested-table read/write-parity case (587). The setup() helper at 431-463 builds the fixture in the body context (no _setEditContextForTest('header')), so these are separate from the header-cell describe at line 292 the finding cited. Assertions are substantive — real summary values ('mixed' vs true) and post-edit document state via store.getDocument() — not mock-call checks, so this is genuine coverage of the new endpoint normalization.

finding.summary: Keyboard toggle now decides from the range for a table cell-rectangle selection, and that path has no test
finding.evidence: `resolveToggle` now calls `isStyleOnInSelection` (text-editor.ts:2895), which walks `visitStyledRunsInRange`; for `range.tableCellRange` that visits every block of every selected cell (range-runs.ts:86-101). Cmd/Ctrl+B over a rectangle of cells therefore changes verdict versus the previous caret-based decision. The new test file never sets a `tableCellRange` (no `tableCellRange` occurrence in backward-selection-toggle.test.ts); the only cell-rectangle tests in the package are for stepSelectionFontSize (editor-step-selection-font-size.test.ts:256) and merge context.

verdict.reason: The finding claims the keyboard-toggle-over-a-table-cell-rectangle path is untested and specifically that backward-selection-toggle.test.ts contains no `tableCellRange`. That is factually wrong: the file sets `tableCellRange` at lines 540 and 564 in two dedicated tests. `backward-selection-toggle.test.ts:535-556` builds a real editor over a real MemDocStore with a 1x2 table, sets a selection carrying `tableCellRange {start:(0,0), end:(0,1)}`, asserts the range summary reads bold=true, dispatches a real meta/ctrl+'b' keydown on the mounted textarea, and asserts every inline of both stored cell blocks ends up `bold === false`. The mirror test at lines 558-578 uses `setup(true, false)` so the left cell is unstyled (rectangle reads mixed) and asserts Cmd+B bolds both cells — covering both directions of the range-derived verdict. The tests are not over-mocked: only canvas/ResizeObserver are shimmed (installCanvasShim, lines 27-66); the editor is the real `initialize()` and assertions read the stored document via `storedCellBlock` (lines 466-469). I confirmed `_setSelectionForTest` forwards the whole DocRange (including `tableCellRange`) into `selection.setRange` at editor.ts:3700-3708, so the flagged branch at text-editor.ts:2905/2924 is genuinely exercised.
